name: What counts as a sandwich?
description: Tests whether the described food qualifies as a sandwich according to the definition supplied in each case. The shared example definition includes fillings between bread slices or inside a split roll, including hinged rolls, and excludes tortillas, wraps, and bowls. Cases cover hot dogs, grilled cheese, tacos, salad, sub rolls, and a beef patty with its own supplied definition. The goal is consistent use of each case’s definition, rather than resolving a universal sandwich taxonomy.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.instructions: Does the food described in `food` count as a sandwich under `definition`? Use only this definition.
questions.yes: The described food satisfies the supplied definition, including a split roll with a hinge.
questions.no: The described food does not satisfy the supplied definition.

stateSchema.label: Sandwich definition
stateSchema.defaultValue: A sandwich is a filling between two slices of bread or inside a split bread roll. A hinged roll qualifies. Tortillas, wraps, and bowls do not.

judgment.rationale: A split roll is explicitly included.

judgment.rationale: Two bread slices with a filling.

cases.name: Taco

judgment.rationale: The definition excludes tortillas.

cases.name: Salad

judgment.rationale: No bread enclosing a filling.

cases.name: Sub roll

judgment.rationale: A filled hinged bread roll qualifies.

name: Distributed-systems experience
description: Tests whether a resume excerpt describes hands-on distributed-systems experience, rather than interest in the topic alone. Positive examples include building a replicated store with consensus and operating cooperating services with messaging and partial-failure handling. Negative examples include a statement of interest and a single-machine application. This checks evidence stated in the excerpt; it does not independently verify the experience or measure overall skill.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.instructions: Does this resume mention experience with distributed systems?
questions.yes: The excerpt describes hands-on work with distributed systems, including multiple cooperating services or nodes, replication, consensus, or distributed data processing.
questions.no: The excerpt does not describe hands-on distributed-systems experience. Interest, a course title, or an unrelated use of distributed is insufficient.

name: Personal information in messages
description: Tests whether a message contains information that identifies or allows contact with an individual under this jeval’s authored definition. The current cases contrast a synthetic personal name/email and phone number with an anonymous complaint and a generic business support mailbox. A generic organizational address alone is negative under these criteria. These examples test the stated boundary rather than establish comprehensive personal-data detection.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.instructions: Does the message contain personally identifiable information?
questions.yes: The text includes information that can identify or contact an individual, such as a full personal name, personal email, phone number, home address, or personal identifier. Synthetic examples still count by their content.
questions.no: The text contains no identifying or contact information for an individual. Generic organizational contact information alone does not count.

name: Room minifridges
description: Tests whether a room description explicitly establishes that a minifridge is available inside the room. Equivalent terms such as “compact refrigerator” should count; a shared refrigerator outside the room or an explicit statement that no minifridge is included should not. The current cases cover direct inclusion, equivalent wording, a shared kitchen, and explicit absence.

questions.name: Question 1
questions.instructions: Does the room have a minifridge?
questions.yes: The description explicitly states that this room includes a minifridge, mini refrigerator, or compact refrigerator available in the room.
questions.no: The description does not establish an in-room minifridge. A shared refrigerator, minibar without refrigeration specified, optional request, or explicit absence is insufficient.

judgment.rationale: Authored synthetic example for user review. Refrigerator is shared and outside the room.

cases.name: Explicit absence

judgment.rationale: Authored synthetic example for user review. Explicitly says there is no in-room minifridge.

name: Sandwich classification — mixed primitives
description: Tests two independent judgments in one request per food: Noul applies the definition supplied in each case to decide sandwich membership; Choice classifies the described physical structure. Copies six cases from What counts as a sandwich? and adds a burrito to cover wraps. Choice labels follow the food description rather than the case name: a folded taco and the described bare beef patty are other. These authored examples are an exploratory answer key, not a universal food taxonomy or validated benchmark.

questions.instructions: Does the food described in `food` count as a sandwich under `definition`? Use only this definition.
questions.name: Is it a sandwich?
questions.no: The described food does not satisfy the supplied definition.
questions.yes: The described food satisfies the supplied definition, including a split roll with a hinge.

criteria.other: Any structure that does not match the other options, including bowls, folded open tacos, and bare patties.
criteria.sliced-bread sandwich: A filling between two separate slices of bread.
criteria.split-roll sandwich: A filling inside a split bread roll, including a hinged roll.
criteria.wrap: A tortilla or flatbread rolled around and enclosing the filling; excludes a merely folded open taco.

questions.instructions: Classify the physical structure described in food, independently of whether definition calls it a sandwich. Use the food description, not the case name. A folded open taco is other; wrap requires a tortilla or flatbread rolled around the filling. Choose exactly one option.

name: Bug severity
description: Illustrative authored bug reports inspired by the Score documentation. Tests whether severity follows functional impact and the availability of a workaround, rather than emotional wording. Scale 0–2; expected values are proposed labels with tolerance 0.5 levels. Review before treating results as benchmark evidence.

criteria: Cosmetic issue only; functionality is unaffected.
A feature is broken or degraded, but an effective workaround is available.
An essential task is blocked and no effective workaround is available.
questions.instructions: How severe is the issue described in report? Judge functional impact and whether an effective workaround is available. Emotional language alone does not increase severity.
questions.name: Bug severity

cases.name: Misaligned export button
PDF export with CSV workaround

severity.rationale: A feature fails, but an effective workaround exists.

cases.name: Safari export failure

severity.rationale: Switching browsers is an available workaround for all affected users.

cases.name: Nobody can sign in

severity.rationale: Essential access is blocked without a workaround.

cases.name: Angry report of cosmetic issue

severity.rationale: Anger does not change the purely cosmetic impact.

name: Support-ticket quality
description: Illustrative authored tickets test how much actionable information a report gives an engineer. Scale 0–3 based on feature identification, reproduction steps and environment details. Severity, tone and length do not determine report quality. Proposed expected levels use tolerance 0.5; all rubric levels are represented.

criteria: No identifiable feature, reproduction steps, or environment; only a vague statement that something is broken.
Identifies the affected feature, but supplies neither reproduction steps nor environment details.
Identifies the affected feature and supplies reproduction steps or environment details, but not both.
Identifies the affected feature and supplies both reproduction steps and environment details.
questions.instructions: How much actionable information does report give an engineer? Rate the presence of an identifiable feature, steps to reproduce, and environment details. Do not infer missing details or substitute severity, emotional tone, or length for those facts.
questions.name: Report quality

quality.rationale: No actionable feature, steps or environment.

cases.name: Feature named

quality.rationale: Names PDF export but supplies neither steps nor environment.

cases.name: Steps without environment

quality.rationale: Provides steps but no browser, operating system or other environment.

cases.name: Environment without steps

quality.rationale: Identifies feature and environment but no reproduction steps.

cases.name: Steps and environment

quality.rationale: Includes feature, reproducible steps and browser/OS details.

cases.name: Long but unhelpful

quality.rationale: Length and anger add no steps or environment.
